definition: A family of fine-tuning techniques that adapt a pretrained model by updating only a small subset or a small additional set of parameters, rather than the full model.
details: PEFT methods (including LoRA, adapters, and prefix tuning) reduce the compute, memory, and storage costs of customizing large models for new tasks or domains.
story: Picture a potter shaping clay on a spinning wheel: every nudge is tiny, but each one is guided by how the last attempt wobbled. Think of it this way: A family of fine-tuning techniques that adapt a pretrained model by updating only a small subset or a small additional set of parameters, rather than the full model. And here is the clever part: PEFT methods (including LoRA, adapters, and prefix tuning) reduce the compute, memory, and storage costs of customizing large models for new tasks or domains. Each pass is a tiny course-correction — the model gets a little less wrong every time. And that is Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning — the quiet loop that turns flailing into skill.
